description: The practical work of keeping people's computers and networks running: the role of IT support, a disciplined troubleshooting method, hardware faults, operating-system and software problems, network connectivity issues, managing users, accounts and printers, and the documentation and customer care that make support effective. Practised on simulated machines and networks in the browser where faults are injected and resolved, mirroring the realities of shared computers, internet cafes and frequent power cuts.
modelledOn: Meyers, CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide
outcomes: Describe the role of IT support and the service desk and how tickets flow and escalate.
Apply a structured troubleshooting method to isolate and resolve a fault.
Diagnose and remedy common hardware faults and power problems.
Resolve operating-system and application issues including boot, update and malware problems.
Diagnose network connectivity problems from the device to the internet.
Manage users, accounts and printers and document work with clear customer care.

units.title: The role of IT support
topics: What IT support does: keeping people productive, not just fixing machines
The service desk, tiers of support, escalation and service-level expectations
Ticketing: logging, categorising, prioritising and tracking a request to closure
Support contexts in Ghana: schools, small businesses, internet cafes and shared computers
Professionalism, confidentiality and safety around electricity and equipment

units.title: The troubleshooting method
topics: A structured approach: identify the problem, form a theory, test, plan, implement, verify, document
Gathering information: questioning the user and reproducing the fault
Isolating a cause by halving the problem and changing one thing at a time
Distinguishing symptoms from root causes; avoiding assumptions
Knowing when to escalate and how to hand over cleanly

units.title: Hardware faults
topics: Inside the PC: power supply, motherboard, CPU, memory, storage and peripherals
Diagnosing no-power, no-boot and POST beep and error codes
Storage faults: failing drives, bad sectors, backups and data recovery basics
Overheating, dust and the effect of a hot, dusty climate on hardware
Power problems: surges, brown-outs, outages, surge protectors and the uninterruptible power supply
Safe handling, electrostatic discharge and basic component replacement

units.title: Operating system and software issues
topics: The boot process and repairing a machine that will not start
Updates, drivers and compatibility problems; rolling back a bad change
Slow or unstable systems: resources, startup programs and disk space
Malware symptoms, removal and the special risk of shared cafe machines
Backups, restore points and reinstalling an operating system as a last resort
Licensing and keeping software legal and patched

units.title: Network connectivity problems
topics: The path from a device to the internet: adapter, cable or Wi-Fi, router, ISP and beyond
IP addressing, DHCP, DNS and the gateway; reading a device's network configuration
Troubleshooting tools: ping, traceroute, nslookup and interpreting their output
Wi-Fi problems: signal, channels, interference and authentication
Diagnosing a dead link versus slow or intermittent service on shared or metered connections
When the fault is upstream: the ISP, a mobile-data outage or a cut submarine cable

units.title: Users, accounts and permissions
topics: User accounts, groups and the principle of least privilege
Password resets, account lockouts and safe identity verification of the requester
File and folder permissions and shared-resource access
Directory services and centrally managed accounts in an organisation
Onboarding and offboarding a user securely

units.title: Printers and peripherals
topics: Printer types and the print path: driver, spooler, queue and device
Diagnosing jobs that will not print, jams, quality problems and connectivity
Shared and networked printers and managing a print queue
Consumables, maintenance and cost control in a resource-constrained office

units.title: Documentation and customer care
topics: Writing clear ticket notes, resolutions and a knowledge-base article others can reuse
Asset inventories, configuration records and standard operating procedures
Communicating with non-technical users: listening, managing expectations and following up
Handling difficult situations, data loss and bad news professionally
Preventive maintenance and user training to reduce repeat problems
Capstone: work a queue of simulated tickets from logging to documented resolution
